Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Software Engineering [IT_4061]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Analyze the key changes that transformed traditional coding practices into modern software               (5)  
  engineering principles. How did these changes influence project scalability?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Apply your understanding of software life-cycle models to demonstrate why iterative and                  (5)  
  incremental models are often preferred over the classical Waterfall model in dynamic business  
  environments.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Analyze how the Spiral model integrates elements of both design and prototyping. What risks does         (5)  
  it aim to mitigate compared to other models?  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Analyze the impact of poor stakeholder communication during the requirement-gathering phase.             (5)  
  How does it affect downstream software quality?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Apply the concepts of cohesion and coupling to demonstrate how they influence the modular                (5)  
  structure and reusability of a software system.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Design a Data Flow Diagram (DFD) for a library management system to illustrate and justify how           (5)  
  key functions and data movements are identified within the system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
4)                Construct a comprehensive DFD for an online ticket-booking system to show the process of refining (5)  
  high-level diagrams into detailed components.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
  B)           Illustrate and analyze how applying design patterns simplifies recurring design problems and             (5)  
  supports scalability in OO systems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

5)                        Evaluate the effectiveness of using activity diagrams to represent system workflows during the early (5)  
  design phase.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
  B)                Evaluate how integrating black-box, white-box, and fuzz testing enhances defect detection            (5)  
  coverage in software products.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"
